correctness.rationale: Connected cographs have unique alternating reduced join/union cotrees; canonical complement-component decomposition proves no duplicates. An independently rewritten exact enumerator built every reduced cotree and globally synchronized 1-WL color signatures for all connected cographs n=1..12, recovering counts 1,1,2,5,12,33,90,261,766,2312,7068,21965; zero indistinguishable nonisomorphic pairs through n11 and exactly three two-element indistinguishable classes at n12 with common degrees 7,8,9. The submitted three explicit pairs have distinct complementary component-size multisets, so are nonisomorphic while each member is regular of identical degree; the original source verifies their placement in exactly those collision classes. Shared-color refinement for n rounds suffices for pairwise equality because a balanced equitable refinement preserves pairwise indistinguishability until proper splits, each consuming at least one of n vertex classes. This is an exhaustive finite proof, not an experiment extrapolated to larger n.
residual_risks: Both enumerators use essentially the same canonical cotree mathematical decomposition although code was independently rewritten.
No result for disconnected cographs or n>12.
